selection_rationale: c1 best matches the track’s requirement for an operationally meaningful, falsifiable study that advances NetOps safety by integrating generation→validation→simulation→rollback; it has high venue relevance, clear primary outcome, and is feasible within the stated compute budget after addressed repairs.
unresolved_uncertainties: U1: Whether LLM-driven agents can safely execute production network changes without human oversight (limited production-scale evidence).
U2: Absence of a community-accepted execution-oriented benchmark that measures end-to-end workflow safety (generation+verification+enactment+rollback).
U3: Robustness of provenance/uncertainty defenses for NetOps RAG pipelines under realistic threat models.
U4: Sufficiency and representativeness of public real-world network-configuration corpora for reproducible large-scale evaluation.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact public corpora to be used and provide a sanitized snapshot or synthetic-equivalent corpus for reproducibility.
Define and validate simulator fidelity versus representative real-world behaviors; document simulator limitations and validation procedure.
Justify single-model choice or include at least one additional model for sensitivity analysis (or predefine why a single-model design is sufficient).
Provide a clear, graded severity/rollback scoring rubric with decision thresholds and examples; pre-register these scoring rules.
Preregister random seeds, retry policy, inclusion/exclusion rules, and explicitly document the simulator/validator interfaces and determinism assumptions.
